environment.tool: manual audit of the tag source + live compiled binary; one client socket per composition, strict-token peer with a monotonic SEQ counter echoed into the body, hex-exact client capture

findings.description: `GET /api%2fexec%20?cmd=id&mode=sub%20n=60` pipelined with a follower: the client's `CL:19` window ends exactly on the exec body (no shift), while the overlong variant reproduces the 29d short-body shape. Any non-zero request `Content-Length` is a 400 at `:53`, so a body-framed follower is impossible on this build.
findings.title: The interim Content-Length becomes `respleft` and the terminal head inherits it, giving the client a wrong body length under a live connection

limitations: Intra-connection only; no cross-client leak was found
Needs an attacker-influenced upstream and a pipelining client
All RCE is RCE on the upstream host
methods: Read the release source from the tag
Diffed the release source against the staged copy (identical)
Exec control and follower control first in the same script
Both request and response direction captured verbatim

author_attested: analysis metadata reconstructed after the run
verified: release tag resolves to the submitted source
source SHA-256 and report and evidence hashes
